Already fixed by 170fe02 (2026-08-05), predating this bead's 2026-08-08 runtime inspection -- the inspected deployment was serving a stale build. el() in ui/src/base/dom.js was treating a falsy scalar first child (0, '', false) as a missing attrs object and dropping it, so any stat tile whose value was 0 (Working now, Needs you, Tokens used before any usage) rendered a blank headline. Fixed with dedicated regression coverage in ui/test/dom.test.js (el renders a falsy numeric value instead of dropping it, statTile renders a zero headline value, etc.) -- all 9 tests pass. Verified ui/dist rebuilds byte-identical to the committed tree, so the fix ships in the current binary. Root cause found after Sam confirmed live testing still showed the task's in-flight tool calls/generation continuing tens of seconds to ~2 minutes after /stop reported success. internal/container/pool.go Release() always slept the configured GracePeriod and always used Docker's default ~10s graceful SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL timeout, even when the release was happening because the task's context had just been cancelled by /stop -- so a cancelled task's container (and the in-flight work inside it) could sit doing nothing for up to GracePeriod+~10s before actually dying. Fixed with a new releaseDecision(ctx, grace) helper: a cancelled ctx now skips the grace sleep entirely and requests an immediate SIGKILL (ContainerStopOptions.Timeout=0) instead of a graceful wait; a live ctx (normal completion) keeps the original behaviour byte-for-byte. Red-then-green with 3 new unit tests (internal/container/pool_test.go), task check clean, adversarially reviewed by a fresh subagent with zero blocking findings -- context-chain trace, Docker Timeout=0 semantics, and struct-equivalence for the unchanged path were all independently verified against the moby client source.

Confirmed root cause: agent containers run as root (no USER in Dockerfile, no userns-remap anywhere in docker-compose.yml/internal/container/pool.go), so a commit the agent writes to the bind-mounted worktree lands owned by UID 0 on the host. The daemon later reads those same loose objects to push, running as its own non-root host user -- 'openat objects/../..: permission denied'. Fixed: containerEnv() now passes the daemon's own os.Getuid()/os.Getgid() as WORKTREE_UID/WORKTREE_GID; hybridTrees.Push (the single choke point before the push RPC) chowns the worktree back to that owner first. Adversarial review (fresh subagent) found one real bug in the first pass -- chownTree used os.Chown, which follows symlinks and fails on a legitimately-tracked-but-dangling symlink, which would have aborted a push that would otherwise have succeeded (worse than the original bug). Fixed with os.Lchown plus a regression test proving it against a dangling symlink. Full task check clean; all other review findings (full-tree walk cost, minor test-hygiene notes) were judged non-blocking by the reviewer.

Superseded: confirmed by Sam that there is no longer a separate /provider command -- grepped the codebase and no '/provider' command exists in internal/gateway or internal/channels/telegram. /model now handles provider scoping directly.

Fixed: configuredMCPProvider (cmd/archied/main.go) now sets NPM_CONFIG_CACHE under the daemon's persistent work_dir and NPM_CONFIG_PREFER_OFFLINE=true for any npx-launched MCP server (matched by base name so an absolute-path npx still qualifies), so a daemon restart reuses a warm npm cache instead of re-resolving/re-downloading from the registry every time -- the amplifier behind the 2026-07-30 crash loop. Guards an empty workDir explicitly (unreachable in production since config defaulting runs first, but matches memoryProvider's existing precedent for the same defense). Adversarially reviewed by a fresh subagent; findings addressed: narrowed an overclaim that this also covers a package's own separate downloads (e.g. Playwright/Puppeteer fetching browser binaries via CDN, which NPM_CONFIG_CACHE does not touch), and closed the absolute-path-command gap. Full task check clean. The identical, arguably-worse instance in internal/app/agentworker/mcp_providers.go (every per-task ephemeral container, not just daemon restarts) needs real new infra -- a persistent Docker volume bind-mounted into task containers, which doesn't exist yet -- so it's filed separately as archie-core-qk8m rather than folded into this scoped fix.
